metadata.title: The Running-Balance Bug Hiding in a Correct-Looking SQL Query
metadata.description: A real SQL correctness bug found and fixed in this book's Chapter 8 worked example: a date filter applied inside the running-balance CTE, before the cumulative SUM() OVER, silently truncating balance history for any account with pre-2026 activity. Fixed by moving the filter downstream to last_posting_per_month.

beats.role_note: why care — stated before the CLI loop begins; SHOW-DON'T-TELL LAW: Manim, not a static card
beats.narration_text: In a bank's data warehouse, 'what's this account's balance today' really means 'sum every posting up to today.' Get that running total right, and the report is trustworthy. Get one clause out of order, and the query still runs, still returns numbers — and every one of them is wrong for any account with history before the reporting window. No error thrown. No warning logged. Just a wrong balance that looks completely correct.
beats.visual_intent: a balance line accumulates smoothly across a 2025→2026 timeline; at the Jan 1 2026 boundary a red gate/cut mark appears with no alarm icon — the line keeps drawing past it uninterrupted, on-screen label 'no error thrown'

beats.role_note: the ordering rule — why the bug is possible at all
beats.narration_text: Here's the rule that explains it. A window function runs after WHERE, GROUP BY, and HAVING — but only inside its own query. Put that WHERE in an earlier CTE instead, and it still runs first, before a SUM() OVER two CTEs downstream ever sees the data. Filter early, and the running total built on top never sees what got filtered out.
beats.visual_intent: split screen: LEFT — ledger rows flow into a filter funnel (rows before 2026 fade away) then into a SUM() OVER accumulator, landing on a small/wrong total, labeled WRONG in crimson; RIGHT — the same ledger rows flow whole into the accumulator first, landing on the true total, THEN a filter narrows to the reporting window, labeled RIGHT in teal. Brace + arrow annotations mark the order on each side.

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL buggy CTE, trimmed to what teaches
beats.narration_text: Here's the CTE that computes the running balance. Read the WHERE clause — it's sitting right inside running, filtering the ledger down to twenty-twenty-six before the SUM() OVER ever runs.

props.title: running_balance.sql (as drafted)
props.code:
WITH running AS (
    SELECT account_id, transaction_id, posted_at,
        SUM(amount) OVER (
            PARTITION BY account_id
            ORDER BY posted_at, transaction_id
            ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING
        ) AS running_balance
    FROM transactions
    WHERE posted_at >= '2026-01-01'   -- <- runs BEFORE SUM() OVER sees it
      AND posted_at <  '2026-07-01'
),
-- last_posting_per_month, monthly_balances, dormant_flag: unchanged

beats.role_note: OPEN vox slot → Manim video — cycle 1, the wrong result
beats.narration_text: Run it against an account that's been open since twenty-twenty-five. The true balance carried twelve thousand four hundred dollars into January. This query says January's balance is negative three hundred. It didn't error. It just forgot the account had a past.
beats.visual_intent: animated result table for ACCT-50231: rows for Jan/Feb/Mar 2026 land one at a time showing -$300.00, -$150.00, -$225.00 in crimson; a pulsing crimson badge reads 'MISSING $12,400 OF HISTORY'

beats.narration_text: That's a bug, not a feature. The fix is one clause, moved one CTE downstream: pull the date filter out of running, and put it on last underscore posting underscore per underscore month instead.

props.command: claude "fix running_balance.sql — the date filter is inside the running CTE, before SUM() OVER runs; move it to last_posting_per_month instead so the running total sees the full ledger"
props.folderLabel: Banking Domain Data Analyst Interview Prep

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL fixed CTE (matches the book's shipped query)
beats.narration_text: Same query, one clause relocated. Running now sees the whole ledger, no WHERE at all. The date filter shows up one CTE later — after the sum is already correct, only narrowing which months get reported.

props.title: running_balance.sql (fixed)
props.code:
WITH running AS (
    SELECT account_id, transaction_id, posted_at,
        SUM(amount) OVER (
            PARTITION BY account_id
            ORDER BY posted_at, transaction_id
            ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING
        ) AS running_balance
    FROM transactions            -- no WHERE — sees the WHOLE ledger
),
last_posting_per_month AS (
    SELECT account_id, DATE_FORMAT(posted_at, '%Y-%m-01') AS month_start,
           running_balance,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
               PARTITION BY account_id, DATE_FORMAT(posted_at, '%Y-%m')
               ORDER BY posted_at DESC, transaction_id DESC
           ) AS rn
    FROM running
    WHERE posted_at >= '2026-01-01'   -- <- filter moved HERE, after the sum
      AND posted_at <  '2026-07-01'
)
-- monthly_balances, dormant_flag: unchanged

beats.role_note: OPEN vox slot → Manim video — cycle 2, the corrected result
beats.narration_text: Re-run it. January's balance comes back as twelve thousand one hundred dollars — the real prior balance, minus the one withdrawal that actually happened in January. Nothing invented. Nothing lost.
beats.visual_intent: mirrored version of B05's table: the crimson -$300.00/-$150.00/-$225.00 rows ghost, strike through, and fade; corrected teal rows land in their place: $12,100.00, $12,250.00, $12,175.00

beats.role_note: the lesson — one beat; SHOW-DON'T-TELL LAW: Manim, not a static card
beats.narration_text: So the bug was never the window function. It was a WHERE clause living one CTE too early. Compute the running total over the whole ledger first. Narrow down to your reporting window only after the balance is already right.
beats.visual_intent: animated checklist, three lines landing with checkmarks: 'Compute the running total over the WHOLE ledger' / 'Filter to the reporting window only AFTER the sum' / 'A misplaced WHERE doesn't error — it quietly zeroes your history'; italic side-note beneath: 'Window functions run after WHERE inside their OWN query — not before a WHERE in an earlier CTE.'
